chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazal, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has not punished a people at all while they were eating, and indeed Allah (Mighty and Majestic) is more Benevolent than that He sustains them with something, then punishes them for it, until they finish it.
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah not punish people while they are eating?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the divine attribute of fairness (Adl), illustrating that punishment is not inflicted for a blessing while it is still being actively enjoyed. It underscores the principle that accountability begins only after the period of grace or consumption concludes, reflecting Allah's generosity in allowing His servants to fully experience His gifts before judgment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazal, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has not Punished a people at all whilst they were eating, and that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is more Benevolent than that He<sup>azwj</sup> Sustains them with something, then He<sup>azwj</sup> Punishes them (whilst they are) upon it, (only after) they are free from it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Faddal from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’

Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has never made a people to undergo suffering while eating food. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, is honorable. He does not give people sustenance, then make them to undergo suffering before they finish eating their food.’”
